algorithm.Title: Nosebleed - Male (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Male
Definition: Nosebleed assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for severe/uncontrolled bleeding, breathing compromise, faintness/shock, major facial/head trauma, or reduced consciousness. Sit forward if alert, spit blood out, and pinch the soft nose continuously. Do not tilt the head back, lie flat, pack the nose deeply, or repeatedly release pressure to check. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Did bleeding begin after a significant facial or nasal injury?
questions.Information: A traumatic nosebleed requires the Nose Injury pathway.

questions.Question: Is there difficulty breathing, reduced consciousness, collapse, faintness or shock, major facial/head trauma, or severe uncontrolled bleeding that is rapidly worsening?
questions.Information: Immediate life-threatening features require Qatar 999. This separates ambulance need from other NHS.UK an emergency assessment service selected through the Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) criteria that may be stable enough for governed non-ambulance transport.

questions.Question: After uninterrupted pinching of the soft nose, has bleeding continued longer than 10-15 minutes, does it still seem excessive, is the person swallowing a lot of blood and vomiting, or did it begin after a blow to the head without the immediate life-threatening features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK directs these features to an emergency assessment service selected through the Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) and says not to self-drive, while allowing either another driver or an ambulance. Exact Qatar destination and transport choice remain GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED.

questions.Question: Is the patient a child under 2, does the caller have regular nosebleeds, anaemia symptoms, take blood-thinning medication, or have a clotting disorder such as haemophilia?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends a clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) for these situations even when the bleed itself has stopped.

questions.Question: Is this a single, brief nosebleed with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes standard first aid as sufficient for an uncomplicated nosebleed.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency nosebleed response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for severe/uncontrolled bleeding, breathing compromise, faintness/shock, major facial/head trauma, or reduced consciousness. Sit forward if alert, spit blood out, and pinch the soft nose continuously. Do not tilt the head back, lie flat, pack the nose deeply, or repeatedly release pressure to check. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: bleeding remains uncontrolled; difficulty breathing, swallowing large amounts of blood, faintness, or shock; major trauma or reduced consciousness.

advice.Title: Urgent in-person nosebleed assessment
Content: Continue sitting forward and pinching the soft nose while arranging prompt in-person emergency assessment through the Qatar governance-approved pathway. Do not self-drive. A safe adult may transport a stable patient only if the approved local pathway permits; call 999 for breathing difficulty, reduced consciousness, collapse, shock, major trauma, or rapidly worsening/uncontrolled bleeding. Exact destination and transport remain GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED.
Call Back If: difficulty breathing, faintness, collapse, or reduced consciousness; bleeding becomes rapidly worse or remains uncontrolled; major trauma.

advice.Title: Routine nosebleed follow-up
Content: Arrange primary-care review through the approved Qatar pathway for recurrent nosebleeds or bleeding-risk factors.
Call Back If: nosebleeds becoming more frequent or heavier.

advice.Title: Home first aid for a nosebleed
Content: Sit down, lean forward with the head tilted forward, pinch the soft part of the nose just above the nostrils for 10-15 minutes, and breathe through the mouth. An ice pack may help.
Call Back If: bleeding continues past 10-15 minutes of pinching; feeling weak or dizzy.
